Test the assumptions behind investment proposals and business cases, constructively and with evidence Find opportunities to grow income, reduce cost and stretch resources without diluting quality 🤝 Build allegiances Work with DCMS, HMRC, museum partners, auditors and professional advisers Influence colleagues, challenge established thinking where it needs challenging, and build real commitment to shared goals Stay plugged into the sector for benchmarking, intelligence and your own development WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR ✅ Essential A professional accountancy qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CIPFA or equivalent) Senior finance experience supporting colleagues across an organisation and reporting to Board level A strong grasp of the concept of the internal customer. You'll be serving and supporting line managers and budget holders with information and other finance needs as well as enabling and supporting their empowerment and independence Experience of leading the annual budget and ongoing forecasting process Experience of leading on the production of statutory accounts and managing the annual audit Previous track record of implementing and developing finance IT systems Evidence of developing effective, efficient policies, processes and controls Experience across a range of sectors, commercial, not-for-profit and public sector Experience of employment taxes, corporation tax and VAT ⭐ Desirable Charity accounting experience Public sector procurement and knowledge of the Procurement Regulations Knowledge of HM Treasury governance and public financial management frameworks — Managing Public Money, the Functional Standards, the Orange Book and the Green Book A background in the cultural or heritage sector (welcome, but not a deal-breaker, there are people around who can teach you the difference between a gauntlet and a vambrace!) WHAT'S ON OFFER 💰 The package Salary c£75,000, on a 18-month fixed-term contract, potential scope beyond this for a candidate with extensive relevant experience Pension scheme with employer contributions of up to 9% 27.5 days' annual leave plus bank holidays Company sick pay scheme 🕓 Hours and flexibility 36 hours per week, 5 days out of 7 Occasional evening, weekend and bank holiday working, this comes with the territory in a museum, not every weekend, but invitations to support new exhibitions and events - a fun benefit! 📍 Where you'll be A hybrid role, Leeds-based, in a building where there's always something interesting happening, with travel to our other sites, very comfortable to support a balance of remote and on-site working Discounted staff parking and the Bike2Work scheme 🍰 The little extras 25% off in the staff shop and 10% off in the on-site café Free online learning and professional development Free Employee Assistance Programme 🚀 READY TO APPLY? The Royal Armouries has been looking after extraordinary objects and extraordinary stories for centuries. The next chapter needs someone who can bring financial rigour worthy of a national museum and enjoy the role while they do it. Closing date 16th October 2026. If that sounds like your kind of challenge, we'd like to hear from you. For a confidential conversation before you apply, please get in touch. The Royal Armouries is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and are happy to discuss adjustments at any stage of the process — the best teams, like the best collections, have always been varied ones.
